name: usePerfetto
summary: Real Android system traces (Perfetto format) of this app, plus os.Trace markers.
plain: Starts and stops a system performance trace and hands back the .perfetto-trace file, viewable in ui.perfetto.dev. Custom trace sections and counters from your code appear inside the trace.
description: startTrace asks the platform for a real Perfetto system trace. On Android 15+ it uses android.os.ProfilingManager: the platform records a trace of this app and delivers the file; its data sources are chosen by the platform, so the categories you pass are not applied (activeCategories stays empty and availableCategories is empty). Where ProfilingManager is absent it runs /system/bin/perfetto with the requested atrace categories, which many devices refuse to let an app execute. When no backend can start, startTrace resolves false and error says why; it never reports a trace that is not recording. stopTrace returns the file path only after checking the file exists with a non-zero size, with its size in lastTraceSizeBytes; otherwise it returns null and sets error. perfettoVersion is read from `perfetto --version` when the app can execute the binary, and is null with perfettoVersionReason otherwise. beginSection, endSection and setCounter use android.os.Trace and are recorded only while a trace is running.

returns.name: isSupported
returns.desc: Whether a trace backend can be started: ProfilingManager (Android 15+) or an executable perfetto binary.

returns.name: isTracing
returns.desc: Whether a trace session is currently recording.

returns.name: perfettoVersion
returns.desc: Version parsed from `perfetto --version`. Null when the app cannot execute the binary; perfettoVersionReason says why.

returns.name: perfettoVersionReason
returns.desc: Why perfettoVersion is null (for example the exec was refused for the app process); null when the version was read.

returns.name: backend
returns.desc: Which backend records traces on this device; null when none is available.

returns.name: availableCategories
returns.desc: atrace categories the perfetto binary accepts. Empty with the ProfilingManager backend, which picks its own data sources.

returns.name: activeCategories
returns.desc: Categories the running trace was configured with. Empty when the backend ignores the request.

returns.name: lastTraceUri
returns.desc: Absolute path of the last saved .perfetto-trace file. Set only when the file exists and is not empty.

returns.name: lastTraceSizeBytes
returns.desc: Size in bytes of the last saved trace file.

returns.name: traceDurationMs
returns.desc: Time between startTrace and stopTrace for the last saved trace, in milliseconds.

returns.name: error
returns.desc: Why the last start or stop produced no trace, or why no backend is available.

returns.name: startTrace
returns.desc: Start a system trace. Resolves false, with the reason in error, when no backend could start one.

returns.name: stopTrace
returns.desc: Stop the active trace. Resolves the file path, or null with the reason in error when no trace file exists.

actions.name: startTrace(categories?, bufferSizeKb?)
actions.desc: Start a system trace with the optional categories and buffer size.
actions.output: Resolves true when a backend accepted the request and reported no failure; false with the reason in error otherwise. With ProfilingManager the categories are not applied and the platform may refuse (rate limit, trace already in progress).

actions.name: stopTrace()
actions.desc: Stop the active trace and verify the .perfetto-trace file.
actions.output: Resolves the absolute path when the file exists with a non-zero size (size in lastTraceSizeBytes); null with error set when there was no trace, the platform delivered no file, or the file is missing or empty.
